measurements.metric_kind: KV-cached DECODE throughput = 1 / median decode-step wall (43 layers, world=64 pure-EP, batch=1; 9-token golden prefill then single-token steps). NOTE: this supersedes the earlier PREFILL-throughput headline (0.029 tok/s) with the standard serving metric (decode).
measurements.milestone: FIRST DeepSeek-V4-family model (284B MoE: MLA + Hyper-Connections + Compressed/Sparse attention + 256-expert FP4 MoE) with real KV-cached decode on Trainium2 native PyTorch, at world=64 pure expert-parallel.
measurements.best_config: world=64 pure-EP (routed experts sharded i%64==rank + all_reduce, shared-after), attention replicated, ALL Linear weights dequantized fp4/fp8 -> bf16 resident ONCE at load (no per-call dequant), KV-cached decode (advancing start_pos, reference decode branch).
measurements.baseline_config: SAME world=64 pure-EP KV-cached decode, but only the routed experts dequantized to bf16; attention + shared-expert weights left fp4/fp8 => dequantized on-device on EVERY forward call (via eager_device_linear).
measurements.baseline_provenance: SELF-MEASURED this session on bigsweep2 (trn2.48xl i-07bcc40b8a7cbbe11), 2026-09-01. Clean same-world=64 A/B: the ONLY difference between baseline and best is whether the non-expert weights are bf16-resident. Not a cross-run or cross-config comparison.
measurements.core_contribution: Localized the decode bottleneck with a per-component breakdown, then fixed it: the attention (675 ms/layer) and shared-expert (161 ms/layer) latency was PER-CALL on-device fp4/fp8 dequantization. Dequantizing all Linear weights to bf16-resident once cuts the 43-layer decode step 38.6s -> 3.393s (11.4x). Post-fix per-layer: attention ~9 ms, shared ~12 ms.
measurements.correctness: argmax=671 at the 9-token golden prompt (matches the prior functional trn2 port and the prefill milestone). Decode token stream deterministic and consistent across runs.
measurements.honest_caveats: Uses world=64 (64 cores) vs the earlier prefill milestone's world=1; but the 11.4x is a FIXED-world=64 before/after (dequant-resident fix only), NOT a core-count artifact. Eager (not compiled). Batch>1 measured to NOT help in eager (BATCH=8: step 3.4s -> 35s, aggregate 0.227 < 0.295 => decode is compute/dispatch-bound, not collective-bound). All-bf16-resident is HBM-tight (23.5 / 24 GB per core; the lm-head is kept bf16 to fit). Reaching the 15 tok/s target needs COMPILED decode (fuse per-layer ops so batching scales sublinearly) + memory reclaim via attention tensor-parallel; both proven feasible this session (a compile-friendly MLA attention compiles at world=64 with a shared-cache + rank-0-first staggered warmup, 3.3x), but a larger integration.
measurements.gate: verified functional KV-cached decode: argmax=671 reproduces the golden; 11.38x is a clean same-world=64 before/after of the bf16-resident dequant fix, both self-measured on bigsweep2 2026-09-01 (median over 3-4 steady decode steps).
